title: Why Do You Feel TWO Noses? (Cross Your Fingers) 🤞
description:
Cross your fingers and rub the tip of your nose in the gap between them: most people feel two noses. Your fingers swapped places, and nobody told your brain. It still treats them as side by side, and a touch on both OUTSIDE edges at once has always meant two separate things. Crossed, those two edges both touch your one nose... so your brain counts two. Aristotle described this trick more than 2,000 years ago, and in a 1991 study volunteers kept two fingers crossed for up to six months, until their brains finally learned the new layout. One nose or two?
